-76.23840,36.73520.name: Procreate Fertility Center of Virginia
-76.23840,36.73520.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Christian Perez, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-71.87870,45.39946.name: Centre de recherche du Centre hospitalier universitaire de Sherbrooke
-71.87870,45.39946.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, February 2026
-71.87870,45.39946.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, February 2026. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-79.88687,-2.19006.name: INNAIFEST - Centro Nacional de Reproduccion Asistida
-79.88687,-2.19006.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: http://www.innaifest.com.ec/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere. No street address resolved, so this point is the city or the country rather than the centre.

14.52344,46.05182.name: The Laboratory for Diagnosis of Zoonoses at the Institute of Microbiology and Immunology
14.52344,46.05182.company: Faculty of Medicine, University of Ljubljana
14.52344,46.05182.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by Faculty of Medicine, University of Ljubljana. It is categorised as a university laboratory, working on animal health. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

174.77560,-41.28660.name: Predator Free 2050 — genetic tools debate
174.77560,-41.28660.desc: New Zealand’s programme to eradicate introduced rats, possums and stoats, and the public argument about whether gene drives should be among the tools. The government funded research and a national conversation before deciding rather than after — which is rare enough in this field to be worth recording either way.

118.79690,32.06030.name: GemPharmatech
118.79690,32.06030.state: Nanjing — 12 Xuefu Road, Jiangbei New Area
118.79690,32.06030.desc: Builds and supplies genetically modified mice at very large scale, with a catalogue of thousands of knockout strains. Founded at Nanjing University and now selling internationally, it is the clearest sign that laboratory-animal supply is no longer a mostly American business.

118.79690,32.06030.name: Nanjing Institute of Environmental Sciences
118.79690,32.06030.desc: The environmental research institute that reported finding genes from the engineered poplars in natural poplar varieties — despite the official position that the commercialised clones were female with altered fertility, which was the reason given for expecting no cross-breeding. A forestry academy official separately observed that the true area of engineered plantation cannot be assessed, because poplar is easy to propagate and sell, material moves between nurseries, and an engineered tree cannot be told from a conventional one by looking at it. Those two findings together are the clearest documented case on this map of a containment assumption failing and the record of where the organism went failing with it.

-80.12400,26.23800.name: US Stem Cell Inc — FDA injunction
-80.12400,26.23800.desc: Injected patients with cells derived from their own fat, including into eyes; three women were blinded. A federal court granted the FDA a permanent injunction in 2019. Hundreds of clinics were operating the same way, selling cell treatments as a service rather than a drug, and enforcement has been case-by-case ever since.

-77.02250,38.89450.name: EPA — plant-incorporated protectant registrations
-77.02250,38.89450.desc: A plant engineered to produce its own insecticide is regulated by the EPA as a pesticide, not by USDA as a crop — the pesticide is the plant. That is why Bt maize carries a registration number and a label with use restrictions, and why resistance management requirements are enforceable against the grower. Anyone trying to find out what a specific engineered crop is permitted to do, or what a grower is obliged to do around it, will find more here than in the release permit.

18.42410,-33.92490.name: Afrigen Biologics
18.42410,-33.92490.desc: Selected in June 2021 by the World Health Organization and the Medicines Patent Pool as the mRNA technology transfer hub, after Moderna and Pfizer declined to provide the know-how to reproduce their vaccines in Africa. Afrigen used the publicly available sequence of Moderna's vaccine to build its own version at laboratory scale — the first vaccine made from a widely used product without the developer's assistance or approval, and the first mRNA vaccine designed and produced on the continent. In 2026 it became the first African facility certified to manufacture investigational biological products for early clinical trials. Its task was to industrialise the platform and transfer it to fifteen partners on four continents. The entry belongs on this map because it is the clearest instance of a genetic technology being rebuilt from a published sequence rather than licensed — the same act the synthesis facet describes as a capability, carried out as policy.
